title: Route canaries and outage detection for managed public and internal routes
problem: A managed service can be healthy at the container level while its user-facing route is broken. On git.sharegap.net, Gitea and grasp-bridge were healthy and nginx accepted its configuration and reloaded successfully, but nginx-git had cached a stale Docker upstream IP after grasp-bridge was recreated and returned HTTP 502 until reloaded by hand. Bahia had no signal: CloudflareBackend.verifyHTTPS runs only at apply time and only for the public edge, and NginxBackend never probed the route at all.
intended_behavior: Bahia treats a managed route as a first-class observable. It probes each route from the public edge and, where configured, from the LAN under split DNS; asserts DNS, TLS trust and expiry, response status and body; classifies failures by the outermost broken layer so a 502 behind valid TLS is reported as an upstream error; blocks or rolls back a deployment whose route fails post-deploy verification; re-probes continuously; and surfaces an open route outage alongside the container-level status of the service behind it.
observed_behavior_before: Route correctness was inferred from provider convergence. nginx -t plus a successful reload was accepted as proof the internal route worked. No periodic route probing existed. No route outage state, lineage, events, or API existed.
non_goals: Detecting the specific provider-internal cause of a stale upstream, which is not externally observable. The operator-actionable fact is that the edge is reachable, TLS is valid, the upstream is broken, and the container is fine.
Making canary expectations part of signed desired state. They are control-plane policy, so changing them must not invalidate a deployed plan hash.
boundaries: Route verdicts never depend on container health; the contrast is joined at the read model and event layer only.
The gate decorates the route lifecycle rather than being spliced into the coordinator, so both the route-only and combined deploy paths are covered by the single apply call each already makes.
TLS verification is never disabled on any probe path.
